newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to set main interest rate weekly.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to set main interest rate weekly.

text.p: Bulgaria is to adjust its main interest rate to market conditions each week instead of each month to meet funding requirements set by the International Monetary Fund in a financial accord signed this week.
"The main interest rate should be determined weekly as the average yield on seven-day discount securities in the previous week," said the accord.

Bulgaria should meet this requirement by the time the first review of a $510 million stand-by agreement with the IMF is carried out, possibly in June, along with introducing a tough fixed exchange rate mechanism, the currency board system.

This year so far the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) has determined the main rate monthly as the average weighted effective monthly yield on one- and four-week discount T-bills auctioned daily by the finance ministry in the month before.
The BNB said in January the rate would change if significant changes in market conditions for one- and four-week securities occurred but has not specified a time period for those changes.
The rate was raised on January 28 to 16.5 percent monthly from 15 percent and from March 1 it was raised further to 18 percent monthly in line with rising yields of government securities.

The Finance Ministry has issued daily discount T-bill issues with maturities of one week and four weeks without par value or a minimum acceptable price set in advance since January 20 to regulate excessive bank liquidity.

Since then the BNB has halted its revrepo operations with maturities of over two days in line with preparations for the introduction of a currency board system under which central bank open market operations would be curbed.

Under the financial accord signed by the IMF and the interim government on Monday repurchase agreement balances should be reduced to zero by end-May, or two weeks before the introduction of a currency board system.

Once the currency board is introduced the BNB will not be able to print levs it cannot cover with hard currency reserves, which is expected to remove political pressure from monetary policy. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 4145
